declaration.question: do clause-structure blocks plus a derived coarse formula beat random blocks and plain annealing on 3-SAT
declaration.statistic: first-hit solved count per n under one budget; median evaluations over solved runs with solved fraction beside it; log2 growth of the median per added variable. AMENDED 2026-10-27 after the --quick run, which saturated solved counts at n<=20 (4/4 in every arm): sizes widened to n=60, k raised to 20, and the median/growth statistics added. The --quick numbers were seen before this amendment
declaration.discriminates: ml_cooc and ml_random share every step except how pairs are chosen, so a gap between them isolates block locality; plain isolates coarse-to-fine as a whole
declaration.expected: if locality matters: ml_cooc solves >= 3/10 more than ml_random at the largest n, or (where both saturate) its median cost is lower by 2x or more. If coarse-to-fine helps at all: ml_cooc >= plain on the same reading. A growth-rate change needs the ml_cooc slope below plain's by more than the spread between seeds; otherwise it is a constant factor

controls.name: coarse solution expands to a fine solution
controls.predicted: every multilevel hit verifies on the original formula
